title: Proof-of-Concept Evaluation of Immunological Assays Using Human Blood and Urine Samples after Vaccination with StroVac
official: Proof-of-Concept Evaluation of Immunological Assays Using Human Blood and Urine Samples after Vaccination with StroVac
summary:
Main objective: 1. To investigate if the ELISA is suitable to detect antibodies (IgG in plasma, IgA in urine) and changes in antibodies against all 10 bacterial strains contained in StroVac induced by StroVac vaccination 2. To investigate if the following methods are suitable for detecting functional antibodies against all bacterial strains contained in StroVac in the blood induced by StroVac vaccination
• opsonophagocytosis assay (OPA) with human plasma
• agglutination test with human serum
• neutralisation test with human serum
conditions: Analytical testing repeated without appropriate rationale

interventions.name: StroVac® Injektionssuspension Wirkstoff: Inaktivierte Keime spezifizierter Enterobakterien

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. The written Informed Consent Form (ICF) has been signed and dated by the patient prior to any trial-related activity.
2. Adult (≥ 18 years) patients with recurrent urinary tract infections who are eligible for treatment with StroVac according to the current SmPC.
3. The treatment decision precedes the decision to participate in the trial and must be independent.
4. Sexually active women of childbearing potential (WOCBP) 1 must use highly effective method of birth control 2 during the trial (from Visit 1 to Visit 4).
Exclusion criteria:
1. Any contraindication according to section 4.3 of the StroVac SmPC
2. Oral or parenteral antibiotic treatment within 7 days prior to Visit 1
3. Vaccination (live or inactivated vaccine) 28 days prior to Visit 1 or plans to receive vaccination during the trial.
4. Females who are breastfeeding
5. A positive pregnancy test indicating pregnancy in a WOCBP at Visit 1 or patient planning to become pregnant during the trial.
6. Any severe (medical) condition (e.g., carcinoma) or any other disease or circumstances that, in the investigator’s opinion, would put the subject at any undue risk, prevent completion of the trial, or interfere with the analysis of the trial results.
7. Psychiatric condition that might limit the participation in the trial and/or that lead to the assumption that the ability to completely understand the consequences of consent is missing
8. In the opinion of the investigator, the patient is unlikely to comply with the trial procedures as defined in the trial protocol.
9. Current participation in any other clinical trial or use of any other IMP within the last 30 days prior to screening visit or within five half-lives of IMP (whichever is longer)
10. Earlier participation in the treatment phase of the trial
11. Drug and / or alcohol abuse
12. Acute urinary tract infection within the last 7 days prior to Visit 1
13. Close affiliation with the investigator (e.g., a close relative, financially dependent on the trial site) or patient who is an employee of the Sponsor’s company.
14. Patients who are institutionalized because of legal or regulatory order.
15. Known infectious diseases (e.g., HIV, HBV, HCV)
16. Blood / plasma donation within the 7 days prior to Visit 1 or planning to donate blood during the trial.
17. Any major surgeries planned during the trial period.
18. Medications known to affect immunological assays within 3 months prior to visit 1
19. NSAIDs of any dose within 24 hours prior to visit 1
20. Anticoagulation treatment within 7 days prior to visit 1
21. Cancer therapies including chemotherapy, radiation therapy, cytotoxic drugs within 6 months prior to Visit 1
